title: Kotlin DSL and Model-Safe Configuration Check

questions.prompt: Which approach best applies kotlin dsl and model-safe configuration?
options: Use public typed models for module intent and move shared configuration behind tested convention plugins.
Configure every subproject from the root
questions.answer: Use public typed models for module intent and move shared configuration behind tested convention plugins.
questions.explanation: The correct approach preserves Gradle’s lazy model, explicit data flow, variant correctness, functional evidence and operability.

questions.prompt: A type-safe Kotlin DSL script is automatically configuration-cache compatible.
questions.explanation: Kotlin compilation can hide architectural sprawl when every module still copies a large, tightly coupled script with subtle divergent defaults.

questions.prompt: Why might a dynamically created model element lack a type-safe accessor?
questions.answer: Accessors are generated from plugins and model elements known before the script body is compiled.
questions.explanation: The answer names the model property that makes the build behaviour predictable rather than relying on incidental script order.
